label: History
value: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls.
unit: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls, feeling a sense of returning home due to his mother's upbringing there. Upon his arrival, Miss Winifred driven him over to meet Nell Harcourt and Lorna Ainslie. He expressed deep excitement about visiting his ancestral home—built by his grandfather John Tremayne—and learning about his family history from Captain Saul Garrick. Over the summer, Adrian collaborated with Captain Saul to write the elderly mariner's life story, taking a photograph of him at the lighthouse doorway for the frontispiece. During his stay, he fell deeply in love with Lorna Ainslie. In August, shortly before his vacation came to an end, Adrian met Lorna in the ancient garden, declared his love, and became engaged to her under the late-blooming red roses. In late September, his published book, titled The Life-Book of Captain Saul, arrived at the post office to the great delight of Captain Saul and their friends.

label: History
value: Ambrose Kerr grew up.
unit: Ambrose Kerr grew up as a passionate Liberal political supporter. During a particularly fierce general election campaign fifteen years earlier, he publicly swore that he would not trim his hair or shave his face until power belonged to the Grits. When his party failed to win, he steadfastly kept his promise, allowing his hair and beard to grow wild for fifteen years and causing local residents and visitors to view him as a eccentric sight. As he reached middle age, he continued cod-fishing and maintained a long-standing acquaintance with Captain Saul Garrick. On the final hour of the old year, Ambrose joined Captain Saul, Dr. Hugh Carrow, Nell Carrow, and Lorna Ainslie to welcome the New Year at the lighthouse. Eventually, he became engaged to Miss Winifred Bryant and agreed to marry her in roughly four weeks, telling her she could wear a wedding veil alongside a navy blue silk gown if she wished.

label: History
value: Anthony Tulk attended Brierley school.
unit: Anthony Tulk attended Brierley school, where he sat alone at a corner desk and exhibited an hostile, sullen attitude toward his teacher, Nell Harcourt. During class, he once poured the remaining water from his slate bottle down the back of Aurelia Clay's neck. When kept in during recess for a lecture on gentlemanly behavior, he remained entirely unmoved and whistled contemptuously upon leaving. On a later occasion, after misbehaving in class, Nell lost her temper and whipped him across the palms with a pointer, causing his defiance to break into tears. Following the whipping, Anthony's attitude shifted completely; he came to respect Nell, remarking that she had some worth despite being a girl and noting that the beating he received from her was as good as a man's. Afterwards, he pardoned her, greeted her politely on the road, and offered to carry her schoolbooks through the snow.

When kept in during recess for a lecture on gentlemanly behavior, he remained entirely unmoved and whistled contemptuously upon leaving. On a later occasion, after misbehaving in class, Nell lost her temper and whipped him across the palms with a pointer, causing his defiance to break into tears. Following the whipping, Anthony's attitude shifted completely; he came to respect Nell, remarking that she had some worth despite being a girl and noting that the beating he received from her was as good as a man's. Afterwards, he pardoned her, greeted her politely on the road, and offered to carry her schoolbooks through the snow.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house
unit: Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house after her only daughter married and departed for missionary work abroad. When her niece Mabel Colby proposed managing a residence for herself, Nell, and Honora while they attended Wexcombe College, Aunt Euphemia agreed to move to Portmaris to act as their housekeeper. At Tabby's Place, she brought along her cat Joseph, which her friend had entrusted to her before moving to Vancouver, and she helped integrate Nell's rescue cat Smudge into the household. Over three winters, she provided a warm, hospitable home filled with firelight, rocking chairs, and pleasant company for the student group. She maintained that while college education could impart wisdom quickly, decades of real life experience had taught her even more.

unit: Barney Pullen escorted Nell Harcourt to a concert at Pale Sands, driving her on the front seat of his buggy and taking immense pride in her presence despite his difficulty maintaining a conversation. Having harbored an infatuation for Nell, he was later gifted the upper farm in his own name by his father. Due to his extreme shyness, he persuaded his sister Odette to propose marriage to Nell on his behalf, offering to wait until she completed her college education if necessary. Nell rejected the proposal, as she had never considered him as a romantic prospect.

label: History
value: Belinda the Fourth serves as a young live-in helper.
unit: Belinda the Fourth serves as a young live-in helper to Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke wander off their path, Miss Rosalind and Belinda host them for tea, serving warm biscuits and mother's wedding china. Unlike the previous Bowman daughters who served as Charlottas, Belinda never mocks Miss Rosalind's pretend tea parties or imaginative games. She holds Nell in total adoration, practicing in her bedroom mirror to imitate Nell's walk, posture, and facial expressions. When wild strawberries ripen in Mr. Kimball's pasture, Belinda invites Nell to join her in picking them for afternoon tea. During this outing, she confides her deep worry to Nell that Miss Rosalind has been sick and lonely ever since taking a cold during a winter evening walk.

label: History
value: Cedric moved from Boston
unit: Cedric moved from Boston to live near the beach with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope, and father. He enrolled at Brierley School under the instruction of Nell Harcourt, becoming a well-liked pupil among both his teacher and fellow classmates. While attending school, he engaged in a notable physical fight with St. Clair Trask over a patriotic dispute regarding their national flags, ending in a mutual pact to respect each other's patriotism. Nell introduced him to Miss Rosalind Penrose at her stone house after learning of Rosalind's past relationship with his father; during the visit, Cedric charmed Miss Rosalind and agreed to become special friends with her. On various occasions, he also visited Grey Shutters for meals.

label: History
value: Hugh teased Nell Harcourt by pulling her crimson braid and calling her "Carrots".
unit: As a boy at Brierley school, Hugh once teased Nell Harcourt by pulling her crimson braid and calling her "Carrots," causing her to break her slate over his head; despite taking the blame for the incident, he was temporarily met with her persistent refusal to forgive him. As he grew up, he developed a deep affection for Nell and strove to live a principled life worthy of her. During his college years at Wexcombe, he led the Freshmen to victory in the annual Arts Rush, was elected class president, and was initiated into the Lambs fraternity after undergoing a humorous public initiation in Portmaris. After one academic year, he offered Mayflowers to Nell and proposed to her, but she turned him down, asking that they remain only friends. He later worked for a newspaper and completed medical training at Portmaris Hospital, ultimately taking over Doctor Dave's medical practice at Seven Gulls Harbor. Eventually, he married Nell, settling with her near the harbor where they enjoyed summer excursions with friends and welcomed the truth regarding Laurence Vane's identity.

unit: As a boy at Brierley school, Hugh once teased Nell Harcourt by pulling her crimson braid and calling her "Carrots," causing her to break her slate over his head; despite taking the blame for the incident, he was temporarily met with her persistent refusal to forgive him. As he grew up, he developed a deep affection for Nell and strove to live a principled life worthy of her. During his college years at Wexcombe, he led the Freshmen to victory in the annual Arts Rush, was elected class president, and was initiated into the Lambs fraternity after undergoing a humorous public initiation in Portmaris. After one academic year, he offered Mayflowers to Nell and proposed to her, but she turned him down, asking that they remain only friends. He later worked for a newspaper and completed medical training at Portmaris Hospital, ultimately taking over Doctor Dave's medical practice at Seven Gulls Harbor. Eventually, he married Nell, settling with her near the harbor where they enjoyed summer excursions with friends and welcomed the truth regarding Laurence Vane's identity.

label: History
value: Isolde attended Brierley School under Miss Thorne.
unit: While attending Brierley School under Miss Thorne, Isolde rehearsed school dialogues such as 'A Morning Visit' alongside Opal Pettigrew and Odette Pullen, and performed a solo song in a student concert. She became best friends with Nell Harcourt, exchanging notes and gifts like red tissue paper bookmarks across the school grounds. During a sleepover at her house, she and Nell accidentally leaped onto a bed occupied by her visiting relative, Aunt Lavinia Pembroke, startling her and causing a stir. Isolde later attended Regent's and subsequently moved on to attend Wexcombe College with Nell. While discussing suitors and future prospects with Nell, she expressed her anxieties about growing older and remaining unmarried.

label: History
value: Lorna completed two years of studies in a single year at Regent's Academy.
unit: After completing two years of studies in a single year at Regent's Academy, Lorna became a joyful and ambitious schoolteacher at the Glen school. That summer, Rufus Vane sought her hand in marriage, but she repeatedly rejected him. However, when Rufus threatened to have his father foreclose on the Ainslie family farm, Lorna sacrificed her own happiness and married Rufus to spare her mother from distress. Following her mother's death a year later and Rufus's departure on the Four Sisters, Lorna remained isolated on the Ainslie farm. After Captain Saul brought back a memory-lacking man identified as Rufus from Havana, Lorna faithfully nursed and cared for him for eleven long years, supporting herself by leasing her farm to John Ward and hosting occasional summer lodgers. She built a warm friendship with Miss Winifred Tolley and eventually with Nell Harcourt. Years later, when medical interest led to investigations of her companion's identity, it was revealed that her husband Rufus had actually died of yellow fever in Cuba, and the man she spent eleven years caring for was his lookalike cousin, Laurence Vane. Upon Laurence regaining his memory, Lorna traveled with him to the hospital to care for him while contacting his family in Nova Scotia.

Years later, when medical interest led to investigations of her companion's identity, it was revealed that her husband Rufus had actually died of yellow fever in Cuba, and the man she spent eleven years caring for was his lookalike cousin, Laurence Vane. Upon Laurence regaining his memory, Lorna traveled with him to the hospital to care for him while contacting his family in Nova Scotia.

label: History
value: Lucy grew up at Grey Shutters.
unit: Lucy grew up at Grey Shutters following the death of her mother, Mary Farrow, living alongside her twin brother Robin under the care of Thirza Abernethy and Nell Harcourt. During her early childhood, she spent her days memorizing Sunday School lessons, assisting with household tasks like shelling peas, and tending her garden plot, while regularly receiving lessons from Nell. Though generally obedient and proper, she was occasionally led into misadventures by Robin, such as ruining her clothes on a pigpen fence, skipping Sunday School, or getting locked in a toolhouse. As she matured through her teenage years, she grew up to inherit Nell's former room at Grey Shutters and formed a courtship with Ralph Pullen.

label: History
value: Mabel attended Regent's Academy.
unit: While attending Regent's Academy, Mabel became part of a close circle of contemplative, creative scholars alongside Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis, winning the Second Year beauty prize. After completing her studies at Regent's, she worked for several years as a country schoolteacher instructing nine grades. Wearying of rural teaching and the misperceptions of her work, she planned to attend Wexcombe College by entering the Sophomore class. She wrote to Nell proposing that they, along with Honora, lease a small house in Portmaris with her Aunt Euphemia as their housekeeper. The plan succeeded, and she moved into Tabby's Place to pursue her final year at Wexcombe.

label: History
value: Nell moved to Grey Shutters.
unit: After moving to Grey Shutters, Nell made a lifelong pact of friendship with Isolde Pembroke in the Pembroke garden. During her school days, she was disciplined by Miss Thorne for secretly reading Ben Hur during Canadian history class, prompting her to promise to avoid foolish novels. When Miss Thorne offered her a place in a preparation class for Regent's entrance exam, Nell eagerly pursued her dream to become a schoolteacher. At Regent's Academy, she was a top contender for the academic medal alongside Hugh Carrow and Penrose Wilson, forming close friendships with Mabel Colby and Honora Hollis. Upon becoming a teacher, Nell firmly resolved never to use physical punishment, striving instead to guide her pupils with kindness and cultivate their inherent goodness as taught by Professor Rennie. Later, she achieved her first literary success when The Youth's Friend accepted a sketch she submitted, earning a ten-dollar check.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy traveled eight miles to Pale Sands Station at Alder River
unit: Obed Abernethy traveled eight miles to Pale Sands Station at Alder River expecting to collect an orphan boy sent from Nova Scotia by Mrs. Alexander Tranter. Upon arriving, he discovered that a young eleven-year-old girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent instead. Too bashful and overwhelmed to correct the mistake directly, he brought Nell home to Grey Shutters so his sister Thirza could resolve the situation. After learning of Nell's history and realizing she might be placed with Mrs. Scobie, Obed strongly advocated for keeping her. Later, noticing that Nell's plain wardrobe differed from her schoolmates' colorful and modern attire, Obed resolved to buy her a stylish dress for Christmas. Overcoming his fear of female store clerks, he ventured to Samuel Lawson's shop in Delford to purchase brown gloria fabric and asked Mrs. Sowerby to sew it into a fashionable gown with puffed sleeves.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer moved to Brierley
unit: After moving to Brierley from New Brunswick, Mr. Pettifer bought the former Bell farm next to the Abernethy home. He quickly earned a local reputation as an eccentric bachelor, eschewing regular meal times, washing his dishes all at once in a rainwater hogshead only on wet Sundays, and refusing to donate money to local church stipends or missionary efforts. He employed John Henry Carter as a farmhand, though he provided irregular meals and criticized his clumsiness. On one occasion, after mistaking his Jersey cow's antics for crop damage, he burst furiously onto the Abernethy property, only to later receive Nell's confession that she had mistakenly sold his stray cow for twenty dollars. Though upset, he managed his temper and restrained his ill-mannered parrot, Nutmeg. Later, Nell confided in him about her ambitions to write a short story, which he received with skepticism, expressing that too much rubbish was already being published.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon was the master of Brierley School.
unit: During his term as master of Brierley School, Mr. Pidgeon was helping Sukey Pullen with algebra when Hugh Carrow provoked Nell Harcourt into smashing her slate over Hugh's head. Intervening in the commotion, Mr. Pidgeon ignored Hugh's admission of fault and made a public spectacle of Nell by forcing her to stand before the blackboard with a chalked inscription reproving her poor temper. The next day, after a sudden impulse to strictly enforce punctuality, he found Nell arriving late alongside the boys. To preserve his reputation without disciplining the whole group, he mocked her and forced her to sit beside Hugh, which caused Nell to leave the school entirely for home instruction. According to local gossip, Mr. Pidgeon was considered a poor instructor who ignored younger children to focus solely on his Regent's candidates and maintained disgraceful discipline, retaining his job only through his uncle's control of the school trustees.

label: History
value: Ezra studied theology at St. Columbia

label: History
value: Robin arrived at Grey Shutters.
unit: Robin arrived at Grey Shutters along with his twin sister Lucy after being taken in by Thirza Abernethy and Nell Harcourt. He started attending school in Brierley and settled into daily household life, though he often disrupted meals and engaged in childish antics such as pulling feathers from roosters or placing a live toad in Thirza's bed. After feeling remorse for his prank, he confessed to Nell so she could safely remove the toad. He experienced jealousy toward Cedric Stanhope, fearing Nell favored Cedric over him, but was comforted when Nell reassured him of her affection. Following the death of his father Richard Farrow, a trust fund was established to secure Robin's and Lucy's upbringing at Grey Shutters. As he grew, Robin engaged in childhood business trades, such as selling his pulled front tooth to Milty Gammon, and proudly declared his childhood betrothal to his classmate Mabel Fletcher.

label: History
value: Rosalind Penrose grew up in an isolated, ivy-draped sandstone house.
unit: Rosalind Penrose grew up in an isolated, ivy-draped sandstone house built by her father near the Welby River. In her youth, she was considered a beauty and became betrothed to Stephen Stanhope; however, after a severe disagreement broke their engagement twenty-five years prior, Stephen left for the United States, and Rosalind gradually withdrew from social life. Residing quietly at Echo Cottage with her young handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth, she remained largely forgotten by the broader community until Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke paid her a visit. During their tea, Rosalind learned that her former fiancé's son, Cedric Stanhope, was being taught by Nell in Brierley. Nell later intercepted the mail to help facilitate a reunion between Stephen and Rosalind. Anticipating Stephen's evening visit, Rosalind dressed nervously in her forget-me-not organdy gown to meet him.

Anticipating Stephen's evening visit, Rosalind dressed nervously in her forget-me-not organdy gown to meet him.

label: History
value: Rufus Vane grew up in the Glen.
unit: Rufus Vane grew up in the Glen as the son of storekeeper Abner Vane. He worked as a clerk during the winter and sailed during the summer. Becoming enamored with Lorna Ainslie, he pursued her despite her repeated rejections. Upon realizing she would not willingly consent, he leveraged his father's mortgage on the Ainslie farm to threaten Mrs. Rose Ainslie with foreclosure, coercing Lorna into marrying him. Following their marriage, he lived with Lorna on the Ainslie property for a winter and planted crops in the spring. Soon growing tired of domestic life, he traveled to Nova Scotia and boarded the ship Four Sisters alongside his double cousin Laurence Vane for a voyage to Havana. While in Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the vessel's departure. For eleven years, his local community mistakenly believed that a brain-damaged man brought back from Havana by Captain Saul was Rufus, until Laurence Vane regained his memory and revealed Rufus's true fate.

Upon realizing she would not willingly consent, he leveraged his father's mortgage on the Ainslie farm to threaten Mrs. Rose Ainslie with foreclosure, coercing Lorna into marrying him. Following their marriage, he lived with Lorna on the Ainslie property for a winter and planted crops in the spring. Soon growing tired of domestic life, he traveled to Nova Scotia and boarded the ship Four Sisters alongside his double cousin Laurence Vane for a voyage to Havana. While in Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the vessel's departure. For eleven years, his local community mistakenly believed that a brain-damaged man brought back from Havana by Captain Saul was Rufus, until Laurence Vane regained his memory and revealed Rufus's true fate.

label: History
value: Tabitha Pratt went to work at the little house of dreams
unit: Tabitha Pratt went to work at the little house of dreams as a servant for Dr. Hugh Carrow and his wife Nell. During her first few weeks, she developed an intense devotion to Nell, whom she called "young Mrs. Doctor." When Thirza Abernethy arrived at the house in June carrying her horsehair trunk, Tabitha initially regarded her with envious suspicion. However, after Thirza refrained from interfering with kitchen duties or Tabitha's care of Nell, Tabitha declared to her friends in the Glen that Thirza was a fine woman who understood her place. During the intense night when Nell went into labor, Tabitha waited in the kitchen with cotton wool stuffed in her ears and her apron over her head. When Thirza expressed fear that the birth might end tragically, Tabitha fiercely rejected the notion that God would rob them of Nell. After the baby girl was successfully delivered and Hugh brought the news downstairs, Tabitha removed the cotton wool and briskly took charge of preparing breakfast for everyone.

value: Thirza Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters.
unit: Thirza Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters with her brother Obed. Expecting an orphan boy from Nova Scotia, she was initially shocked when Obed returned with an orphan girl named Nell Harcourt. Although uncertain about raising a young girl, Thirza agreed to keep Nell after considering it her duty and taking pity on her circumstances. Despite initially struggling with Nell's emotional outbursts and vivid imagination, Thirza defended Nell against harsh criticism from neighbor Agatha Sowerby. Over the years, Thirza diligently trained Nell into a composed, dependable young woman. Later in life, she took her very first long journey away from home to visit Seven Gulls and spend Christmas with the newly married Nell and Hugh Carrow.

At the end of June, her reign at Brierley School concluded. On her last day, she delivered moving farewell remarks to her students. Before the Entrance examinations, she escorted candidates including Nell, Odette, Opal, and Flossie to the Academy, having advised them beforehand to avoid late-night cramming.
